cur:manuscripts-augustine-gospels-luke-c.summary: Saint Luke sits enthroned beneath an arch with his winged ox, and between the columns on either side twelve tiny scenes drawn from his Gospel rise in stacked compartments. In several of them the haloed Christ appears — teaching, in a boat with his disciples, and calling Zacchaeus down from the sycamore tree at the bottom right. The portrait thus presents the evangelist surrounded by the Christ whose story he tells.
facts: When King Charles III was crowned in 2023, the Gospels were carried in the procession open at this very page with the portrait of Luke.
The manuscript once had a portrait and a page of narrative scenes for each evangelist; only those for Luke survive.
cur:manuscripts-augustine-gospels-luke-c.notes: The individual identifications of the small side scenes vary between scholars; captions were added later in England.

cur:monumental2-faras-hodegetria.summary: Two surviving fragments preserve the upper part of the Virgin's mantle and, at the top, the Christ Child seated on her arm: a frontal boy with large dark eyes and a cross-inscribed halo, holding a scroll and blessing. Below, the Virgin's long purple-brown robe falls in heavy vertical folds to a footstool. The type, in which Mary presents her Son to the viewer, is known as the Hodegetria, 'she who shows the way'.
facts: The painting was removed from the walls of Faras Cathedral during the Polish excavations of 1961–64 directed by Kazimierz Michałowski, part of the UNESCO Nubian Campaign before the area was flooded by Lake Nasser.
The National Museum in Warsaw holds 67 paintings from Faras; the cathedral's walls bore several superimposed layers of painting from the 7th to the 14th century.

cur:objects-makk-cologne-book-cover-chri.summary: On the left leaf of this book cover Christ sits in majesty on a footstool, holding a book and blessing, while the twelve apostles are seated around him in tiers, turning toward him in discussion. The right leaf carries openwork scrolls with medallions of the evangelist symbols. The composition presents Christ as Teacher among the apostolic college, the source of the Gospel the book contains.
facts: The museum dates the cover to the 10th century; the lattice and scroll frames are carved in openwork so that the wood or a coloured ground would show through (type).
